Source of truth: packages/ui/src/primitives, the live /design-system page (open it first), and references/." --- # Kortix Design System **Track this file:** `.agents/skills/kortix-design-system/SKILL.md` **If you are touching a visual surface in `apps/web`, follow this.** This file owns **which component to compose**. It does not own values — see below. > **Read [`kortix-brand`](../kortix-brand/SKILL.md) first.** > It is the router for the Kortix look and voice. Its visual files > (`color.md`, `typography.md`, `layout.md`, `effects.md`, `motion.md`) are the > value law: the closed allowlist for every color, spacing step, type rung, > radius, elevation, easing and duration, plus the rule on **whether to animate > at all**. Its `decisions.md` records why each rule is what it is. This file > assumes you know those values and shows you what to build with them. ## Companion skills — load all three | Skill | Owns | Wins when they conflict | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | | [**kortix-brand**](../kortix-brand/SKILL.md) | The value allowlists, voice and claims. Color, spacing, type, radius, elevation, motion budget. Rejected defaults. `scripts/audit.sh`. Decision history. | **Values, copy and motion restraint** | | **kortix-design-system** (this file) | Components, layout shells, reference implementations, banned primitives | **Which component** | | [**make-interfaces-feel-better**](../../../apps/web/.agents/skills/make-interfaces-feel-better/SKILL.md) | Polish: concentric radius, optical alignment, tabular nums, hit areas, font smoothing | **Polish detail** | A polish skill will always propose more motion than Kortix wants. `kortix-brand` is the ceiling all three operate under. Corrections to earlier versions of this file (the shadow ladder that never existed, the press value) are recorded in [`decisions.md`](../kortix-brand/references/decisions.md), entries E1 and E2. ## The product look: read this before you lay out anything Kortix product UI is a quiet, persistent system, not a set of pretty one-offs. The look comes from discipline that repeats on every screen, not from decoration. When a recipe below covers your screen, copy its structure and classes (never its example data). When a later section of this file disagrees with this one, this section wins. ### Measure in real pixels Kortix sets `--spacing: 0.23rem`: one spacing step is 3.68px, not 4px. Every size class is 8% smaller than stock Tailwind. Measured: `h-8` 29px, `h-10` 37px, `h-11` 40px, `h-12` 44px, `w-5` 18px, `w-16` 59px, `w-28` 103px, `w-32` 118px, `w-36` 132px, `w-72` 265px. `text-xs` is 13px, about 7px per character. Size a column from these numbers, never from a stock-Tailwind habit. ### The ten laws 1. **Dense inside, calm outside.** Rows are compact (`text-sm` names, `text-xs` meta, `h-11` rows). The space between blocks is large and empty. Never compensate for a thin page with a big centered column, a hero title or padding. 2. **Hierarchy from ink and size, not from color, boxes or weight.** Three ink roles, nothing else: - **Name ink:** `text-foreground`, `font-normal`. Field values, and the names of rows that need attention (Needs review, Failed) or are selected. A live row is marked by its glyph, not by bright text. - **Title ink:** `text-foreground font-medium`. The page `

`, a section heading, the selected row's name. At most one per row. - **Meta ink:** `text-muted-foreground`. Everything else: labels, timestamps, counts, context, descriptions, people, branches, durations. Meta ink is the default. Bright text is the exception: at most about a third of the visible names. **A row in a live or resting group (Running, Done, Archived) and a routine feed event write their name in meta ink too**, at the same size and geometry: the eye goes to the live work first. **Rail values are meta ink too**, except the status word: the rail is reference, not work. No `font-semibold` in product chrome below a detail-view title. No opacity on text (`text-foreground/60`). 3. **Edges are hairlines, not fills.** A group, a section and a list are separated by `border-border` 1px rules or by space. Never a filled bar (`bg-muted`) as a group header. Never a bordered panel around bordered inputs. Never a card per row. Count the nested boxes: more than one outline around any piece of text is a defect. 4. **Color only means state.** Hue appears only on a state glyph for a live or attention state (running, needs review, failed) and on diff counters, from `STATUS_TEXT` in `@kortix/ui/status`. A resting state (done, idle, archived) is meta ink: ten green checks down a list are noise, and the group header already says "Done". A person, a model, a trigger, an event type and a count never carry a hue. **No `UserAvatar` in product chrome outside a participant stack and a comment author:** its fill is a hashed hue. A person in a row, a rail or a field is their name in the ink the slot prescribes. Diff counters are the `DiffStat` primitive (`@kortix/ui/status`, ``), never hand-built spans. The checked `Switch` is the one accent outside status; it is the primitive's, never restyle it. **An agent's name carries its pixel mark everywhere it appears** (page title, breadcrumb, agent rows, pickers): `AgentMark` from `@kortix/ui/internal/components/agent-mark`, `size={14}`, `shrink-0`, `gap-1.5` before the name. It is the agent's face, not a decoration; rail and facts-grid values still carry no glyph. **An object's own state words differ from its children's.** An agent or a trigger is Active, Paused or Archived; Running, Needs review and Done are the words of its sessions or runs. Never label the parent "Running", and a parent and its children never share a glyph or a hue: in a list row, the parent's Active is a `size-2 rounded-full bg-current` dot in meta ink (it is the normal state, not news; the rail shows only the word), Paused is `PauseCircleIcon` and Archived is `ArchiveIcon`, both in meta ink. `CircleDashedIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.success` belongs to a child that runs now; green on a page means "running" and nothing else (diff counters aside). 5. **One grid per page.** One horizontal inset for every row, group header, tab bar and section on the page: `px-3`, the same as the page header. One row height per list. **One leading slot** (`flex w-5 shrink-0 justify-center` plus the row's `gap-3`) on every row AND every header, so all text starts on one x. A header with no caret keeps the slot empty. Trailing columns have fixed widths, so values line up down the page. Every list on every tab of one page uses the same row. **A page has exactly two text edges:** chrome text (breadcrumb, tab labels, settings labels) starts on the inset (`px-3`, 11px), and list text (group headers, row names) starts on the inset plus the leading slot (about 40px). Measure the breadcrumb, the first tab label and a row name at 1440px: a third x value is a defect. 6. **The name owns the row.** The name column keeps at least half the row at every width. At most three trailing columns (an actor, and for objects that run, the duration and the relative end time). At most ONE secondary fact sits inline after the name (a branch or an ID, never a duration), in meta ink. Columns appear by the list's own width, never truncating at the same time as the name: the inline fact from `@xl/list` (576px), the people column from `@3xl/list` (768px). The name is `max-w-full shrink-0 truncate`, so the fact gives up its space first. Identifiers (branches, repo slugs, IDs, paths) are `font-mono text-xs text-muted-foreground` on every surface: rows, feed context, rail, facts line. Never sans in one place and mono in another. Every row of one list carries the same inline fact or none. What hides below `lg` stays reachable on the row's destination. Never two columns from one fact (a duration and "12 minutes ago"), and never two facts in one column: a time column holds one value type in one format on every row. For objects that run (sessions, runs) it is the duration: elapsed time for a live row (`42m`), the final run length for an ended row (`22m`), `tabular-nums`; the exact start and end times are in its `InlineMetaTime` hint. For objects that do not run (docs, spaces) it is the relative time of the last change (`6m ago`). Never mix `8m` and `6m ago` in one column. An actor column holds actors only: a person's name, or an automation with a `size-3.5` meta-ink glyph before its name (`ClockIcon` Schedule, `WebhooksLogoIcon` Webhook), so the two kinds read apart. The cell is `flex items-center gap-1.5` with a `size-3.5 shrink-0` slot on every row (an empty `` for a person), so the text of the column starts on one x. A trailing column is as wide as its longest realistic value: the people column is `w-36` (132px): after its `size-3.5` slot and `gap-1.5` it holds about 16 characters of `text-xs`. Render the longest name in your data and confirm it has no ellipsis. A value that is not a person in a people column is one word ("Schedule", "Webhook"). A name that truncates at 1440px is a defect. **Nothing in the rail or the facts grid truncates:** prose wraps (`whitespace-normal break-words`) and identifiers wrap too (`font-mono text-xs whitespace-normal [overflow-wrap:anywhere]`). Only list rows truncate. 7. **Say it once.** The page header names the page. The body never repeats the name as a big heading with a description under it. A row never repeats its group (under a "Yesterday" header a row shows `09:14`, not "yesterday"). No title over description over title. One sentence per empty state, at most 60 characters, so it fits 2 lines in `EmptyState size="sm"`. 8. **States keep the shape.** Loading draws the loaded layout in `Skeleton` (recipe below): same group headers, same row height, every column slot at its width. Counts and tabs stay mounted in every state and keep their width, so nothing shifts. On a first load nothing is known: a count is a `Skeleton` in the count's slot and a fact that comes from the list is a `Skeleton` too; never an invented value. **A tab's count slot never unmounts:** the trigger holds a fixed `inline-flex w-6 justify-end` slot; loaded puts `CountBadge` in it, loading a `Skeleton h-3 w-5 py-0`, and error the last known `CountBadge`, or a meta-ink `–` on a first-load error (the slot keeps its width and the underline ends at a glyph, never at blank space). Tab labels sit at the same x in all four states. Creating an object from any state shows the loaded list with the new row and the new count before the success toast. Empty and error states sit in the list area. 9. **Real data, specific copy.** Specific names, real identifiers, clock times. Copy is short and declarative, with no filler and no trailing period on titles. When a side panel shows one object, its row is the open row (`bg-active`, name in title ink); a page with no side panel has no open row. Copy that names an object reads it from the current data, so a rename updates it. Acronyms are uppercase in every string, mock titles included (API, CI, PR, SDK). State words keep their label case in prose ("Moved to Done"). An error names the user-level cause and what still works ("Release Captain keeps running its sessions."), never a status code or a retry count. 10. **Motion is feedback, not decoration.** Hover is a color change (`transition-colors duration-fast`). Lists appear at once. Nothing on a product page animates on load. ### Page width: by page type | Page type | Content frame | | --- | --- | | List page (spaces, sessions, triggers, an inbox) | Full width of the pane, rows `px-3`, no `max-w-*`. A centered column truncates names and wastes 40% of the screen. | | Detail page (a trigger, a goal, a space, an agent) | Full width: main column `min-w-0 flex-1` + a properties rail `w-72 border-l` at `lg:`. The work gets the width; the facts sit in the rail. | | A settings tab inside a detail page | Left-aligned on the page inset: `w-full max-w-2xl px-3 pt-6 pb-16`, the rail stays. No `mx-auto`, no `py-10`. | | A standalone settings page, a customize section | `mx-auto w-full max-w-2xl px-4 py-10` (the shell under "Layout & responsiveness"). | The content of a list or detail page starts directly under the header row: the tab bar or the first group header is the next line. ### Leading glyphs: one style, one glyph per state Every leading glyph is a Phosphor icon at `size-4` in the `w-5` slot, at the global weight (never a `weight` prop). One fixed glyph per state, never a per-row pattern or seed: | State | Glyph | Ink | | --- | --- | --- | | Running, live | `CircleDashedIcon` | `STATUS_TEXT.success` | | Needs review, awaiting you | `GitPullRequestIcon` (code) or `EyeIcon` (anything else) | `STATUS_TEXT.warning` | | Failed | `XCircleIcon` | `STATUS_TEXT.destructive` | | Queued, idle | `CircleIcon` | meta ink | | Done | `CheckCircleIcon` | meta ink | **Feed events have a closed glyph table** (all `size-4`, meta ink unless a colour is given): | Event | Glyph | | --- | --- | | Started | `PlayIcon` | | PR opened | `GitPullRequestIcon` | | Asked for review | `GitPullRequestIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.warning` | | Merged | `GitMergeIcon` | | Finished | `CheckCircleIcon` | | Failed | `XCircleIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.destructive` | | Edited | `PencilSimpleIcon` | Never `GitBranchIcon` for a PR event. **One glyph, one ink, one meaning, on the whole page.** A state glyph keeps its state ink everywhere it appears, list or feed: "Asked for review" in the feed is the Needs review glyph in `STATUS_TEXT.warning`. No other event borrows a state glyph outside the table above. **One hue, one meaning:** blue is the checked `Switch` ("on") and nothing else on a page; orange is "awaiting you"; green is "running"; red is "failed". `ArrowSquareOutIcon` means "opens outside the app" and nothing else. List every glyph across all tabs before you hand back; each maps to exactly one meaning. `SolidCheckIcon` is the completion confirmation that swaps in after an action (copy → copied); it is not a row state. `SessionDotMatrix` marks live work in the session view, not in a list's leading slot. ### Recipe: list rows with groups Example domain: the runs of a scheduled trigger. Copy the structure, not the words. ```tsx const LEAD = 'flex w-5 shrink-0 justify-center'; // The one separator, used in rows, feeds and facts. No spaces or flex gap around it. const SEP = ·; // The list fills the main column:
{groups}
// No max-w-*: every hairline in the main column spans the tab bar's width, up to the rail.
{/* the toggle is only caret + name + count; column captions sit outside it */} {/* first group only: captions in the value slots */} {/* the caption carries the value's glyph slot, so its text starts on the values' x */} Started by Duration Ended
{open ? (
  • {/* no gap-*: SEP's px-1.5 is the only space around the dot */} {/* name ink only for attention groups (Needs review, Failed); meta ink for live and resting groups */} {/* the name never shrinks below its text; the fact takes what is left */} Post the weekly churn report to #revenue {SEP}run_8f2c41 {/* a person gets */} Schedule 2m 14s {/* relative z-10 lifts the hint trigger above the stretched link; the hint shows the exact time */} 14m ago
) : null}
``` - Every row of an object list is one link (`after:absolute after:inset-0`) with the hover fill, so the whole row is clickable and keyboard focusable. In mock code, link to the route the object would have (`/projects//runs/`). A row menu (⋯) is a sibling with `relative z-10`, see "List page rows" below. The row whose object is open beside the list shows `bg-active` and its name in title ink. - Rows inside a group have no divider: the 40px rhythm and the hover fill separate them. Only the group header (`border-b border-border`) and the pane edges draw a hairline. A rule every 40px reads as ruled paper. - Rows sort by the group's time column: a live group by longest elapsed first, every other group by most recent change first. - The people column shows whenever the list itself is at least 48rem wide (`hidden @3xl/list:flex`), decided by the list's width, not the viewport. - The first group header carries the trailing column captions ("Started by", "Duration", "Ended") in meta ink, in the same slots as the row values, outside the toggle button (a caption is not a control). Later group headers leave the slots empty. A caption's text starts on the same x as its values' text (measure: more than 1px off is a defect). - **A cell never states something false.** A live row's "Ended" cell is a meta-ink `–` with `aria-label="Still running"`; its elapsed time is already in Duration. Never "now", never "running". Read every cell aloud with its caption ("Ended: now"): a false sentence is a defect. - The group name is `text-foreground font-medium` inside an `h2` that names the group's `
`; the caret, the count and the captions are meta ink. Each value cell carries its caption for screen readers (`Duration `). - A row has one Tab stop: its link. At most one hint per row is focusable, and it holds every exact time (started and ended) in one `Hint`. - Creating an object expands its group, scrolls the new row into view (`scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })`), focuses its link, and only then calls `successToast`. - The time column holds one value type (law 6). Rows sort by it: a live group by longest elapsed first, other groups by most recent end first. - Group order is the order of urgency: the group that waits on the user first (Needs review, Failed), the live group second (Running), resting groups last (Done, Archived). Only the attention group uses name ink. - A collapsed group keeps its header. A group with no rows is not drawn. - Group counts are bare `tabular-nums` meta text. `CountBadge` is for a tab or a nav item, not a group header. ### Recipe: an activity feed The same row and the same group header (without the caret: the slot stays, empty). Example domain: a project's documents. ```tsx
  • Edited:{' '} {/* routine event: object in meta ink; attention event (Failed, Asked for review): object in text-foreground */} Pricing FAQ {SEP} rev 14 {/* a Finished event's context is */} 09:14
    • ``` - **Every event glyph is meta ink.** Only a failure colors its glyph (`STATUS_TEXT.destructive`). "Started", "merged", "opened" are past events, not live states: never green, never the running glyph. - **One type size per line:** the event phrase and the object are both `text-sm`; only a mono identifier is `text-xs`. - **One grammar for every row:** `:` in meta ink, then the object's name, then ` · ` and one context fact. The colon keeps an imperative title from gluing onto the verb: "Moved to review: Pin the SDK in white-label apps", "PR opened: Bump the API client to 2.14", "Failed: Backport the webhook retry". Never "Merged Tag web 4.8.0…". - **A closed vocabulary before the colon:** Started, Pushed, PR opened, Merged, Finished, Failed, Asked for re

A person in a row, a rail or a field is their name in the ink the slot prescribes. Diff counters are the `DiffStat` primitive (`@kortix/ui/status`, ``), never hand-built spans. The checked `Switch` is the one accent outside status; it is the primitive's, never restyle it. **An agent's name carries its pixel mark everywhere it appears** (page title, breadcrumb, agent rows, pickers): `AgentMark` from `@kortix/ui/internal/components/agent-mark`, `size={14}`, `shrink-0`, `gap-1.5` before the name. It is the agent's face, not a decoration; rail and facts-grid values still carry no glyph. **An object's own state words differ from its children's.** An agent or a trigger is Active, Paused or Archived; Running, Needs review and Done are the words of its sessions or runs. Never label the parent "Running", and a parent and its children never share a glyph or a hue: in a list row, the parent's Active is a `size-2 rounded-full bg-current` dot in meta ink (it is the normal state, not news; the rail shows only the word), Paused is `PauseCircleIcon` and Archived is `ArchiveIcon`, both in meta ink. `CircleDashedIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.success` belongs to a child that runs now; green on a page means "running" and nothing else (diff counters aside). 5. **One grid per page.** One horizontal inset for every row, group header, tab bar and section on the page: `px-3`, the same as the page header. One row height per list. **One leading slot** (`flex w-5 shrink-0 justify-center` plus the row's `gap-3`) on every row AND every header, so all text starts on one x. A header with no caret keeps the slot empty. Trailing columns have fixed widths, so values line up down the page. Every list on every tab of one page uses the same row. **A page has exactly two text edges:** chrome text (breadcrumb, tab labels, settings labels) starts on the inset (`px-3`, 11px), and list text (group headers, row names) starts on the inset plus the leading slot (about 40px). Measure the breadcrumb, the first tab label and a row name at 1440px: a third x value is a defect. 6. **The name owns the row.** The name column keeps at least half the row at every width. At most three trailing columns (an actor, and for objects that run, the duration and the relative end time). At most ONE secondary fact sits inline after the name (a branch or an ID, never a duration), in meta ink. Columns appear by the list's own width, never truncating at the same time as the name: the inline fact from `@xl/list` (576px), the people column from `@3xl/list` (768px). The name is `max-w-full shrink-0 truncate`, so the fact gives up its space first. Identifiers (branches, repo slugs, IDs, paths) are `font-mono text-xs text-muted-foreground` on every surface: rows, feed context, rail, facts line. Never sans in one place and mono in another. Every row of one list carries the same inline fact or none. What hides below `lg` stays reachable on the row's destination. Never two columns from one fact (a duration and "12 minutes ago"), and never two facts in one column: a time column holds one value type in one format on every row. For objects that run (sessions, runs) it is the duration: elapsed time for a live row (`42m`), the final run length for an ended row (`22m`), `tabular-nums`; the exact start and end times are in its `InlineMetaTime` hint. For objects that do not run (docs, spaces) it is the relative time of the last change (`6m ago`). Never mix `8m` and `6m ago` in one column. An actor column holds actors only: a person's name, or an automation with a `size-3.5` meta-ink glyph before its name (`ClockIcon` Schedule, `WebhooksLogoIcon` Webhook), so the two kinds read apart. The cell is `flex items-center gap-1.5` with a `size-3.5 shrink-0` slot on every row (an empty `` for a person), so the text of the column starts on one x. A trailing column is as wide as its longest realistic value: the people column is `w-36` (132px): after its `size-3.5` slot and `gap-1.5` it holds about 16 characters of `text-xs`. Render the longest name in your data and confirm it has no ellipsis. A value that is not a person in a people column is one word ("Schedule", "Webhook"). A name that truncates at 1440px is a defect. **Nothing in the rail or the facts grid truncates:** prose wraps (`whitespace-normal break-words`) and identifiers wrap too (`font-mono text-xs whitespace-normal [overflow-wrap:anywhere]`). Only list rows truncate. 7. **Say it once.** The page header names the page. The body never repeats the name as a big heading with a description under it. A row never repeats its group (under a "Yesterday" header a row shows `09:14`, not "yesterday"). No title over description over title. One sentence per empty state, at most 60 characters, so it fits 2 lines in `EmptyState size="sm"`. 8. **States keep the shape.** Loading draws the loaded layout in `Skeleton` (recipe below): same group headers, same row height, every column slot at its width. Counts and tabs stay mounted in every state and keep their width, so nothing shifts. On a first load nothing is known: a count is a `Skeleton` in the count's slot and a fact that comes from the list is a `Skeleton` too; never an invented value. **A tab's count slot never unmounts:** the trigger holds a fixed `inline-flex w-6 justify-end` slot; loaded puts `CountBadge` in it, loading a `Skeleton h-3 w-5 py-0`, and error the last known `CountBadge`, or a meta-ink `–` on a first-load error (the slot keeps its width and the underline ends at a glyph, never at blank space). Tab labels sit at the same x in all four states. Creating an object from any state shows the loaded list with the new row and the new count before the success toast. Empty and error states sit in the list area. 9. **Real data, specific copy.** Specific names, real identifiers, clock times. Copy is short and declarative, with no filler and no trailing period on titles. When a side panel shows one object, its row is the open row (`bg-active`, name in title ink); a page with no side panel has no open row. Copy that names an object reads it from the current data, so a rename updates it. Acronyms are uppercase in every string, mock titles included (API, CI, PR, SDK). State words keep their label case in prose ("Moved to Done"). An error names the user-level cause and what still works ("Release Captain keeps running its sessions."), never a status code or a retry count. 10. **Motion is feedback, not decoration.** Hover is a color change (`transition-colors duration-fast`). Lists appear at once. Nothing on a product page animates on load. ### Page width: by page type | Page type | Content frame | | --- | --- | | List page (spaces, sessions, triggers, an inbox) | Full width of the pane, rows `px-3`, no `max-w-*`. A centered column truncates names and wastes 40% of the screen. | | Detail page (a trigger, a goal, a space, an agent) | Full width: main column `min-w-0 flex-1` + a properties rail `w-72 border-l` at `lg:`. The work gets the width; the facts sit in the rail. | | A settings tab inside a detail page | Left-aligned on the page inset: `w-full max-w-2xl px-3 pt-6 pb-16`, the rail stays. No `mx-auto`, no `py-10`. | | A standalone settings page, a customize section | `mx-auto w-full max-w-2xl px-4 py-10` (the shell under "Layout & responsiveness"). | The content of a list or detail page starts directly under the header row: the tab bar or the first group header is the next line. ### Leading glyphs: one style, one glyph per state Every leading glyph is a Phosphor icon at `size-4` in the `w-5` slot, at the global weight (never a `weight` prop). One fixed glyph per state, never a per-row pattern or seed: | State | Glyph | Ink | | --- | --- | --- | | Running, live | `CircleDashedIcon` | `STATUS_TEXT.success` | | Needs review, awaiting you | `GitPullRequestIcon` (code) or `EyeIcon` (anything else) | `STATUS_TEXT.warning` | | Failed | `XCircleIcon` | `STATUS_TEXT.destructive` | | Queued, idle | `CircleIcon` | meta ink | | Done | `CheckCircleIcon` | meta ink | **Feed events have a closed glyph table** (all `size-4`, meta ink unless a colour is given): | Event | Glyph | | --- | --- | | Started | `PlayIcon` | | PR opened | `GitPullRequestIcon` | | Asked for review | `GitPullRequestIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.warning` | | Merged | `GitMergeIcon` | | Finished | `CheckCircleIcon` | | Failed | `XCircleIcon` in `STATUS_TEXT.destructive` | | Edited | `PencilSimpleIcon` | Never `GitBranchIcon` for a PR event. **One glyph, one ink, one meaning, on the whole page.** A state glyph keeps its state ink everywhere it appears, list or feed: "Asked for review" in the feed is the Needs review glyph in `STATUS_TEXT.warning`. No other event borrows a state glyph outside the table above. **One hue, one meaning:** blue is the checked `Switch` ("on") and nothing else on a page; orange is "awaiting you"; green is "running"; red is "failed". `ArrowSquareOutIcon` means "opens outside the app" and nothing else. List every glyph across all tabs before you hand back; each maps to exactly one meaning. `SolidCheckIcon` is the completion confirmation that swaps in after an action (copy → copied); it is not a row state. `SessionDotMatrix` marks live work in the session view, not in a list's leading slot. ### Recipe: list rows with groups Example domain: the runs of a scheduled trigger. Copy the structure, not the words. ```tsx const LEAD = 'flex w-5 shrink-0 justify-center'; // The one separator, used in rows, feeds and facts. No spaces or flex gap around it. const SEP = ·; // The list fills the main column:
{groups}
// No max-w-*: every hairline in the main column spans the tab bar's width, up to the rail.
{/* the toggle is only caret + name + count; column captions sit outside it */} {/* first group only: captions in the value slots */} {/* the caption carries the value's glyph slot, so its text starts on the values' x */} Started by Duration Ended
{open ? (
  • {/* no gap-*: SEP's px-1.5 is the only space around the dot */} {/* name ink only for attention groups (Needs review, Failed); meta ink for live and resting groups */} {/* the name never shrinks below its text; the fact takes what is left */} Post the weekly churn report to #revenue {SEP}run_8f2c41 {/* a person gets */} Schedule 2m 14s {/* relative z-10 lifts the hint trigger above the stretched link; the hint shows the exact time */} 14m ago
) : null}
``` - Every row of an object list is one link (`after:absolute after:inset-0`) with the hover fill, so the whole row is clickable and keyboard focusable. In mock code, link to the route the object would have (`/projects//runs/`). A row menu (⋯) is a sibling with `relative z-10`, see "List page rows" below. The row whose object is open beside the list shows `bg-active` and its name in title ink. - Rows inside a group have no divider: the 40px rhythm and the hover fill separate them. Only the group header (`border-b border-border`) and the pane edges draw a hairline. A rule every 40px reads as ruled paper. - Rows sort by the group's time column: a live group by longest elapsed first, every other group by most recent change first. - The people column shows whenever the list itself is at least 48rem wide (`hidden @3xl/list:flex`), decided by the list's width, not the viewport. - The first group header carries the trailing column captions ("Started by", "Duration", "Ended") in meta ink, in the same slots as the row values, outside the toggle button (a caption is not a control). Later group headers leave the slots empty. A caption's text starts on the same x as its values' text (measure: more than 1px off is a defect). - **A cell never states something false.** A live row's "Ended" cell is a meta-ink `–` with `aria-label="Still running"`; its elapsed time is already in Duration. Never "now", never "running". Read every cell aloud with its caption ("Ended: now"): a false sentence is a defect. - The group name is `text-foreground font-medium` inside an `h2` that names the group's `
`; the caret, the count and the captions are meta ink. Each value cell carries its caption for screen readers (`Duration `). - A row has one Tab stop: its link. At most one hint per row is focusable, and it holds every exact time (started and ended) in one `Hint`. - Creating an object expands its group, scrolls the new row into view (`scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })`), focuses its link, and only then calls `successToast`. - The time column holds one value type (law 6). Rows sort by it: a live group by longest elapsed first, other groups by most recent end first. - Group order is the order of urgency: the group that waits on the user first (Needs review, Failed), the live group second (Running), resting groups last (Done, Archived). Only the attention group uses name ink. - A collapsed group keeps its header. A group with no rows is not drawn. - Group counts are bare `tabular-nums` meta text. `CountBadge` is for a tab or a nav item, not a group header. ### Recipe: an activity feed The same row and the same group header (without the caret: the slot stays, empty). Example domain: a project's documents. ```tsx
  • Edited:{' '} {/* routine event: object in meta ink; attention event (Failed, Asked for review): object in text-foreground */} Pricing FAQ {SEP} rev 14 {/* a Finished event's context is */} 09:14
    • ``` - **Every event glyph is meta ink.** Only a failure colors its glyph (`STATUS_TEXT.destructive`). "Started", "merged", "opened" are past events, not live states: never green, never the running glyph. - **One type size per line:** the event phrase and the object are both `text-sm`; only a mono identifier is `text-xs`. - **One grammar for every row:** `:` in meta ink, then the object's name, then ` · ` and one context fact. The colon keeps an imperative title from gluing onto the verb: "Moved to review: Pin the SDK in white-label apps", "PR opened: Bump the API client to 2.14", "Failed: Backport the webhook retry". Never "Merged Tag web 4.8.0…". - **A closed vocabulary before the colon:** Started, Pushed, PR opened, Merged, Finished, Failed, Asked for review, Edited. A value (a duration, a count, a version) never goes in the phrase: it is the context fact after ` · `, or nothing. Consecutive events on one object within 10 minutes collapse into the later one. - **A feed records state changes, not steps.** At most two events per object per day: its latest transition and, if different, its start. "Started" shows only for an object that is still running. Pushes fold into the next PR opened, Merged or Asked for review. At least half the rows are transitions (Asked for review, Merged, Finished, Failed). - **An attention event** (Failed, Asked for review) writes its OBJECT name in name ink and keeps the phrase in meta ink, with the state glyph: the phrase repea

---
name: kortix-image
description: "Recipe: produce a Kortix image (hero, OG card, social card, thumbnail, cover, blog image, illustration, UI asset). Load kortix-brand first. This skill covers sizes, tools, generation, compositing and export. Use when the user asks to create, art-direct or revise an image for Kortix, agents, sandboxes, coding workflows, launch assets, thumbnails or covers."
---

# Kortix image recipe

Turn a visual request into one clean, brand-safe image.

**Load [`kortix-brand`](../kortix-brand/SKILL.md) first.** It owns the values, the voice, the claims and the logo rules. This file owns the procedure only. If a request conflicts with the kit, say so and offer the closest on-brand option.

Output PNG by default. Output SVG only when the user asks for SVG.

## Read before you start

| Need | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Direction, avoid list, reject list, share-card template | [`art-direction.md`](../kortix-brand/references/visual/art-direction.md) |
| Which logo file, recolor, one mark per surface, composite rule | [`brandmark.md`](../kortix-brand/references/visual/brandmark.md) |
| Color and the one-accent rule | [`color.md`](../kortix-brand/references/visual/color.md) |
| Words in or beside the image (headline, caption, in-image text) | [`voice-and-tone.md`](../kortix-brand/references/verbal/voice-and-tone.md), [`claims.md`](../kortix-brand/references/verbal/claims.md), [`positioning.md`](../kortix-brand/references/verbal/positioning.md) |

Settle the context below. Default from the kit and the request. Ask only what changes the art direction.

- **Image goal.** Type (blog hero, social graphic, product mockup, banner, brand asset, OG image), placement (website, social, directory, app store, email) and dimensions.
- **Production approach.** Existing brand assets to use, photoreal or illustrative, one-off or reusable template.
- **Technical.** Available image tools and keys (Gemini, Replicate or Flux, Ideogram), budget, and whether the image needs web optimization.

## Specs

Generate at the native size of the surface. Keep critical content crop-safe.

- OG and blog hero: **1200 by 630** (1.91:1)
- X post: **1200 by 675** (16:9). X header: **1500 by 500**
- LinkedIn post: **1200 by 627**. LinkedIn personal cover: **1584 by 396**
- Square (Instagram, launch card): **1080 by 1080**. Story or reel: **1080 by 1920** (9:16)

Pin the aspect ratio in the prompt. A forgotten ratio is the most common cause of unusable output.

## Tools

- **General generation.** Gemini or Flux.
- **A consistent set.** Flux multi-reference.
- **Text that must live in the image.** Ideogram renders text best. Prefer the default: composite real text in Roobert after generation.
- **Product UI.** Never generate it. Screenshot the real Kortix UI at 2x and frame it.

## Workflow

1. Confirm the surface, the aspect ratio and any required text or facts.
2. Write one short prompt: subject, Kortix product truth, direction from `art-direction.md`, composition, aspect ratio. Keep it tight. Over-specifying produces worse images.
3. Generate as PNG. Composite the official logo file and any exact text after. Follow `brandmark.md`.
4. For the web, also export an optimized WebP (about 80% quality). Set explicit width and height to avoid layout shift. Add descriptive alt text.
5. Reject, and do not ship, any image that matches the reject list in `art-direction.md`.
6. Report the files you read and a "Guesses" list, as `SKILL.md` of `kortix-brand` says.

skills.body:
--- name: kortix-presentation description: "Recipe: build, edit, present or record a Kortix deck or film (a Next.js route under /presentations in apps/web, never a file). Load kortix-brand first. This skill covers the slide engine, builds, presenter notes, films and QA. Load WHENEVER the user asks for a deck, slides, a presentation, a walkthrough, a talk track, a guided demo, presenter notes, or a product video; and whenever editing anything under apps/web/src/app/[locale]/presentations." --- # Kortix Presentations **Load [`kortix-brand`](../kortix-brand/SKILL.md) first.** It owns color, type, layout (deck column), motion, voice and claims. This file owns the slide engine and the procedure. **A Kortix deck is a Next.js route.** Every presentation lives at `/presentations/` in `apps/web`, styled like the marketing site, driven by the keyboard, and built to be screen recorded. There is no file format. Do not produce `.pptx`, Keynote, Google Slides, or a Markdown "slides" file — that output gets rejected on sight, and nothing in this skill will help you make one. A deck is a React component: it themes correctly, stays sharp at any projection size, is reviewed in a PR, and cannot drift from the product copy because it imports the same content modules the marketing pages do. ## Where everything is ``` apps/web/src/app/[locale]/presentations/ layout.tsx full-bleed shell, noindex page.tsx the index — every deck, one card each index-client.tsx the index UI (client: reads each deck's slides for counts) registry.ts the ONE file you edit to add a deck [deck]/ page.tsx server route: generateStaticParams + generateMetadata deck-client.tsx resolves slug → deck, mounts the engine decks/.tsx a deck: `useSlides(): SlideDef[]` engine/ deck.tsx keyboard engine, build steps, presenter notes, overview parts.tsx Slide, SectionHead, Spine, Panel, RowList, Shot, Rise… diagram.tsx build-aware mechanism diagrams README.md the authoring guide this skill summarises ``` Shipped decks: `security` (diagram-led — **the reference implementation, read it first**), `platform`, `sales`. Legacy `/presentation` paths 307 to their new homes via `next.config.ts`. The tree is allowlisted public in `src/middleware.ts` — decks are link-shared and `noindex`, never behind a login. ## Using a deck Open `/presentations`, pick one, press `F`. | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | `→` `Space` `J` | next build step, or next slide | | `←` `K` | back one step, or previous slide fully built | | `Home` `End` | first / last slide | | `1`–`9` | jump to slide | | `G` `Esc` | overview grid (every slide, fully built) | | `F` | fullscreen | | `N` | presenter notes — the spoken script | **Recording:** open the deck, press `F`, record the tab. Read the script first with `N` → **Full script**, then close the drawer — notes never render on the stage, so the recording stays clean. Prefer light theme on decks that embed product screenshots, since the screenshots are light. Reload before you record: after a hot reload in dev, accumulated keydown listeners make one press jump several steps. ## Films — launch and product videos A video is not a screen recording of a deck. It is a **film**: a route at `/presentations/film/` where every frame is a pure function of the frame number. The same React tree plays live (it is the hero of `/launch`) and renders to MP4 through headless Chrome and ffmpeg, with a synthesized score and sound effects locked to the bar grid (60 fps, 120 BPM, one bar = 120 frames). ```bash open http://localhost:/presentations/film/launch # live, scrubbable open "http://localhost:/presentations/film/launch?frame=1800" # one frame bun apps/web/scripts/film/render.ts launch --url http://localhost: # 1080p60 MP4 bun apps/web/scripts/film/render.ts launch --url http://localhost: --audio-only ``` The MP4 lands in the gitignored `output/film//`. Never edit a film file while a render runs: hot reload reaches the render pages. The engine, the storyboard, the motion rules, the sound pipeline and the verification bar: **`references/films.md`**. Read it before touching a film. ## Adding a deck — two edits **1. `decks/.tsx`** — a client component exporting `useSlides()`: ```tsx 'use client'; import type { SlideDef } from '../engine/deck'; import { Slide, Rise, Spine, Panel, Dim } from '../engine/parts'; export function useSlides(): SlideDef[] { return [ { id: 'title', label: 'Chapter name', notes: 'What you say while this is on screen.', node: (

The claim

), }, ]; } ``` **2. A row in `DECKS` in `registry.ts`:** ```ts { slug: 'connectors', title: 'Connectors walkthrough', description: 'One line for the index card and the route metadata.', kind: 'Product', tags: ['Diagram-led'], useSlides: useConnectorsSlides, } ``` There is no step 3. The route, the index card, the slide and build counts, the length estimate and the page metadata are all derived from those two edits. ## The slide API ```tsx type SlideDef = { id: string; // stable, unique within the deck label: string; // shown bottom-left on the stage node: ReactNode | ((step: number) => ReactNode); steps?: number; // extra build steps. Total → presses = steps + 1 notes?: string | readonly string[]; // the spoken script }; ``` ## Builds — the format Kortix decks use `steps: 3` means `→` is pressed four times on that slide, and `node(step)` lights up one more part of the picture each time. Advancing past the last step moves on; reversing off step 0 lands on the previous slide at *its* last step, so `←` always undoes exactly what `→` just did. This is the point of the format: **a diagram assembles while it is explained, instead of landing all at once.** Reach for it whenever you are explaining a mechanism — a request crossing a boundary, a branch becoming a merge, a call being held and released. **The hard rule: never mount or unmount on a build step.** Every element is in the DOM from the first frame, ghosted, and a step raises its opacity. If parts appeared instead, every press would reflow the slide and the viewer would lose the thread. ```tsx // ✅ opacity — layout is stable, the eye tracks what changed
= 1 ? 'opacity-100' : 'opacity-15')}> // ❌ conditional render — the slide jumps on every press {step >= 1 ? : null} ``` `engine/diagram.tsx` does this for you via its internal `Reveal`. The one deliberate exception is a travelling packet (`Link fire`), which is genuinely transient and mounts for its step only. ## Presenter notes `notes` is what you *say*, not what is on screen. Pass an array to give each build step its own line; the drawer follows the step you are on. skills.name: kortix-release
skills.desc: How to cut a Kortix production release — the versioning philosophy (when patch vs minor vs major) and the exact flow: one Promote to Production dispatch takes the dev HEAD through staging to a release PR into prod, whose one release suite is the only gate; fix forward on dev until it is green, then merge and verify prod. Load WHENEVER the user wants to release, promote, cut/ship a version, publish a release, bump the version, or asks why a promotion is stuck. Load it too whenever another skill or doc needs to describe the release/promotion flow — this file is the one place it is written out in full.
skills.body:
---
name: kortix-release
description: "How to cut a Kortix production release — the versioning philosophy (when patch vs minor vs major) and the exact flow: one Promote to Production dispatch takes the dev HEAD through staging to a release PR into prod, whose one release suite is the only gate; fix forward on dev until it is green, then merge and verify prod. Load WHENEVER the user wants to release, promote, cut/ship a version, publish a release, bump the version, or asks why a promotion is stuck. Load it too whenever another skill or doc needs to describe the release/promotion flow — this file is the one place it is written out in full."
---

# Kortix Release

How a clean, accurate production release happens. Three parts: **what version**
(the bump philosophy), **how a candidate gets tested** (one Promote dispatch takes
the `dev` HEAD through staging to a release PR; its one release suite is the
only gate), and **how prod gets it** (merge → deploy → verify). The release notes you write become the GitHub Release, which
the public **`/changelog/releases`** page (Release history) renders as written, and the
weekly **`/changelog`** page merges by section (New / Improved / Fixed) into the
week the release was published — so they must reflect what actually shipped,
nothing invented, nothing missed.

Pairs with **kortix-voice** (how the notes read) and **kortix-rollback** (the
reverse direction). The version source of truth is the root **`VERSION`** file;
`vX.Y.Z` tags are immutable and map 1:1 to a commit + image.

This file is the single source of truth for the promotion flow. `AGENTS.md`
(`CLAUDE.md`), `.agents/skills/contributing/SKILL.md`, and
`.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` state only their own slice — what CI runs on
a PR into `dev` versus the release PR — and point here for the rest.

## 0. Golden rule — one dispatch, one suite, one gate

**The only normal way to change prod is one Promote to Production dispatch.**
It takes the `dev` HEAD, merges it into `staging` itself (a PR that runs
nothing), waits until staging serves that SHA, and opens the release PR into
`prod`. That PR runs the **release suite** once: the contract lanes on the
release tree, the deployed smoke and the browser journeys against staging,
CI, CodeQL and the scanners. Its check `full suite + quality gates` requires
every one of them green, and it is the only check that blocks anything
(testing reset, 2026-10-16). Never `git push …:prod`, never open a manual PR
into `prod`, never cherry-pick onto `prod`.

Nothing else tests the release tree: no `Tests` run on a push to `dev`, no
check on the PR into `staging`. Staging is the deploy target the suite runs
against, not a test stage. The nightly `Tests` run on `dev` (contract lanes,
no browser) warns early: check it before you promote, and fix `dev` forward
when it is red, because the release suite fails on the same lanes.

`dev` is the dev trunk. It can move fast and can temporarily be broken.
Production promotion always reads from `staging`.

## 1. Versioning philosophy — what bump?

Semver `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. **Default to patch.** When unsure, patch.

- **Patch** (`1.0.0 → 1.0.1`) — the everyday release. Bug fixes, small features,
  copy, docs, infra, polish. **This is most releases.** Ship often; keep them small.
- **Minor** (`1.0.x → 1.1.0`) — a milestone worth signposting: a meaningful batch of
  new user-facing capability. Use sparingly, when a release is genuinely "a thing."
- **Major** (`1.x → 2.0.0`) — a breaking change or an architecture shift (the kind of
  jump v0.x → 1.0 was). Rare.

If the change set is "fixes + a couple small features" → **patch**. Don't inflate.

## 2. The flow (do this every time)

### Step 1 — `dev` takes verified merges; the nightly run warns

`dev` takes PRs with no required CI: the developer verifies the change by
using it (the **testing** skill). A push to `dev` runs no `Tests` lane. The
nightly run on `dev` (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`, 05:41 UTC) comments a red
result on the commit. Fix it forward on `dev`, or revert the culprit after 1 hour.

### Step 2 — check the nightly run and cost migrations

```bash
gh run list --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --workflow tests.yml --branch dev --event schedule \
  --limit 1 --json conclusion,headSha --jq '.[0]'
```

A red night means fix `dev` first. Then cost every new migration (Step 5)
before you dispatch: Promote applies it to the staging database within minutes.

Then run the release suite's fast tripwires on the `dev` SHA you promote:

```bash
git fetch origin dev && git switch --detach origin/dev   # in your own worktree
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && bash scripts/pre-promote-tripwires.sh
```

It takes about 2.5 min. It names each red check, and you fix each one on
`dev` before the dispatch. v0.15.11 needed 3 release-suite runs (about 1 h
each) for failures this script finds in minutes (the learnings ledger,
2026-11-14).

The script runs no DB suite and only a few package tests. When the last
nightly is red, or `dev` moved since it ran, also run the contract lanes on
the `dev` SHA you promote (about 15 min) and fix every red lane first:

```bash
gh workflow run tests.yml --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --ref dev
```

v0.16.5 found 6 reds this way that the script missed (the learnings ledger,
2026-11-24).

### Step 3 — one dispatch: Promote to Production

Write the title and notes (Step 7 shows how), then:

```bash
gh workflow run promote.yml --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --ref dev \
  -f ref=dev -f title="<title>" -f notes="$(cat <<'EOF'
<markdown notes>
EOF
)" -f bump=patch
```

Promote then:

1. Resolves `ref` (default `dev`) to a SHA and pushes it to
   `promote/dev-<sha10>`. On a conflict with `staging` it builds the branch as
   a merge whose tree equals the dev SHA's tree (`git read-tree --reset -u`).
2. Opens the PR into `staging` and merges it as a merge commit (never squash).
   That PR runs no check.
3. Dispatches `build-staging.yml` for the merge SHA (a merge made with the
   workflow token starts no push workflow), waits for Build and Deploy
   Staging, then needs 8 consecutive `/health` reads where API, gateway and web
   all serve the merge SHA.
4. Creates or updates `release/vX.Y.Z`, opens the PR into `prod`, and approves
   the held runs on it, so the release suite starts.

`-f dry_run=true` prints every decision (SHA, conflict, PR, version) and
changes nothing. `-f ref=staging` skips the dev leg: the hotfix path for a
commit already on `staging`.

**A failed promote resumes.** When the run fails after the staging merge
(build, deploy or the `/health` proof), fix the cause and re-run the run (or
dispatch again with the same `ref`). The plan step finds the merged
`promote/dev-<sha10>` PR; while its merge is still the staging tip it skips the
merge, skips the build when the three staging manifests already passed, and
always repeats the 8-read `/health` proof. When staging moved on after that
merge, use `-f ref=staging`. A re-promote cancels the gate run of the release
PR's older head itself.

### Step 4 — the release suite is the gate; fix forward

Merge only when `full suite + quality gates` is green on the release PR's head
SHA. Never fix on the release or promotion branch, and never weaken a check
(the fix-forward traps are in
[references/fix-forward-traps.md](references/fix-forward-traps.md)).

**The candidate is frozen on `staging`.** A red suite is fixed on the tree
that was promoted, not on a newer `dev`: every re-promote from `dev` pulls in
new merges, and on 2026-10-28 five cycles in a row each failed on new `dev`
drift (Marko: "pin it to whatever got promoted to staging & fix it on staging
until it's green"). Per fix:

1. Merge the fix into `dev` through a PR, as usual, so `dev` keeps it.
2. Cherry-pick that commit onto `staging` through a PR:
   `git switch -c stage-fix/<slug> origin/staging && git cherry-pick <dev sha>`.
   Then regenerate the generated files on that branch and commit any change:
   `bash .agents/skills/learnings/scripts/index.sh` and
   `node packages/ui/scripts/gen-i18n-catalog.mjs`. `dev`'s copy can list an
   entry or a key from a commit that `staging` lacks (the learnings ledger,
   2026-11-02). Push, `gh pr create --base staging`, `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   The push to `staging` starts Build Staging and Deploy Staging.
3. When `/health` on the three staging surfaces serves the new staging SHA,
   dispatch `promote.yml -f ref=staging` (no `dev` leg). It updates the
   release branch, and the suite runs once on the new tree.

The next normal Promote from `dev` merges cleanly: `dev` already holds every
fix that `staging` got.

### Step 5 — cost every new migration against prod, before merging

For every migration file new in the diff versus what's already applied to prod
(`select name from kortix_migrations.pgmigrations order by id desc limit 5;` on
the real prod database), run it read-only against prod first:

```bash
PGOPTIONS='-c default_transaction_read_only=on -c statement_timeout=15000' \
  psql "$PROD_DATABASE_URL" -c "explain (analyze, buffers) <the migration's statement, read-only form>"
```

Get exact row counts, table size, and lock profile for the target table before
judging a migration safe. Pre-build any large `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` out of
band on prod, with the migration's **exact** statement, so the real deploy step
is a no-op (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` on an index that already
exists does nothing). If the deploy step still hits `55P03` (lock timeout),
**retry by rerunning the migration job** — never by raising `lock_timeout` in a
plain migration (the **learnings** ledger, "Retry a hot-table ADD COLUMN that
hit its 2 s lock_timeout; never raise the timeout", 2026-09-25). Full costing
method: §4 "Gotchas" below and `packages/db/MIGRATIONS.md`.

### Step 6 — staging deploy

Promote dispatches `Build Staging Artifacts`, which starts `Deploy Staging`:
it applies pending migrations to the staging database and rolls staging.
Promote waits for the proof itself; to check by hand:

```bash
curl -fsS https://staging-api.kortix.com/v1/health | jq '{environment,version,commit}'
curl -fsS https://gateway-staging.kortix.com/health/live | jq '{version,commit}'
```

The gateway's `/health` answers only `{status}` to an anonymous caller
(`apps/llm-gateway/src/health.test.ts`); `/health/live` carries the version.
The staging web sits behind Vercel Authentication: an anonymous read of
`staging.kortix.com/api/health` gets `302`. Promote reads it with the Vercel
bypass from AWS Secrets Manager. All three must report the exact SHA you
promoted. Deploy Staging runs list the `dev` SHA as their head: match the
deployed SHA by `/health`, not by the run's `headSha`. A staging runtime check that
points at `dev.kortix.com` / `dev-api.kortix.com` is a broken staging setup, not
a passing gate.

### Step 7 — open the release PR

Derive the title and notes from the **full** commit log since the last release —
not from memory:

```bash
git fetch origin --tags --quiet
PREV="$(git tag -l 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1)"
git log "$PREV..origin/dev" --no-merges --pretty='- %s (%h)'
```

- **title** — one human line, sentence case, outcome-first
  (e.g. `"Warm pool, billing fixes, and a faster session boot"`).
- **notes** — markdown bullets grouped loosely (new / improved / fixed),
  user-facing changes first, internal/infra commits folded into plain outcomes.
  Follow **kortix-voice**: plain language, no hype, "open source" never a
  license name. Every notable commit in the log maps to a line in the notes;
  nothing invented, nothing dropped — the notes are the public `/changelog`.

Then run:

```bash
Dispatch Promote with them (Step 3).

`promote.yml` **creates the `release/vX.Y.Z` PR into `prod` once**, then on every
later dispatch **updates the branch in place** (pushes the new content, keeps
the same PR). **It does not rewrite an already-open release PR's title or
body** — if the version, title, or notes need to change after the PR exists,
edit them by hand with `gh pr edit`. GitHub holds the bot-opened PR's
`tests-release.yml` run (`action_required`); `promote.yml` then approves it.
Only that pull request run's `full suite + quality gates` counts for the `prod`
ruleset. A dispatched run on the same SHA does not (v0.13.57: green dispatched
gate, PR still `BLOCKED`), so never dispatch a second gate. If the Promote
summary warns that approval failed, approve it yourself:
`gh api -X POST repos/kortix-ai/CompanyOS/actions/runs/<run id>/approve`.

### Step 8 — release gate triage

`tests-release.yml`'s `full suite + quality gates` job is the only *required*
check in the repository (on the PR into `prod`). Until 2026-10-06 staging's API
ran in `us-west-2` and its database in `eu-west-2`, so the owner decision of
2026-09-29 classified a `503 request_deadline` (55 s) or a flow timeout on the
release gate as **environmental**. Since 2026-10-06 both run in `eu-west-2`, so
that cross-region reason no longer holds: confirm with the owner before you
classify a timeout as environmental. Every other failure is fixed on
`dev` and re-promoted with one new dispatch (Step 3). A failed gate run reruns its failed jobs once by
itself (`rerun-failed-once.yml`) and names them on the release PR. A job that
fails twice is real. A job that passes on the rerun is a flake: fix it or
delete it (the **testing** skill) in the same release cycle; nothing is quarantined. A shard that
never gets past its own bootstrap gives no signal: it is rerun like any other.

### Step 9 — prod

Merge the release PR once `full suite + quality gates` is green on its head
SHA **and** one team member approved it. Since 2026-10-23 the `prod` ruleset
(20587235) requires 1 approving review with `require_last_push_approval`: an
approval counts only for the last push, so a re-promote that updates the
release branch needs a new approval. Under the SOC 2 Change Management Policy
the person who releases may approve the release PR themselves: one click, and
that approval authorizes the release (decision of 2026-10-23). Approve as soon
as the gate goes green. Never bypass the review. The one exception is an
emergency rollback or fix: an admin bypass then needs an after-the-fact
approval comment by a second person within 2 business days (compliance rule
CM-3).

```bash
gh pr merge <release-pr> --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --merge
```

Never add `--admin` to merge over a red or missing gate unless the owner
approves that exact release in the conversation. Over v0.13.45 to v0.13.56, 9 of
12 releases merged that way, and a gate that is bypassed by habit stops
catching anything.

Confirm a `Deploy Prod` run exists for that merge SHA and succeeds, then verify
every surface on the new version:

```bash
curl -fsS https://api.kortix.com/v1/health | jq '{environment,version,commit}'
curl -fsS https://gateway.kortix.com/health/live | jq '{version,commit}'
curl -fsS https://kortix.com/api/health | jq '{version,commit}'
npm view @kortix/sdk version
npm view @kortix/agent-tunnel version
npm view @kortix/llm-catalog version
gh release view "vX.Y.Z" --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --json name,body,assets --jq '{name,assetCount:(.assets|length)}'   # 24 assets
for i in api gateway frontend; do for t in X.Y.Z prod; do curl -fsS "https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/kortix/kortix-$i/tags/$t" | jq -r --arg t "$i:$t" '"\($t) \(.digest)"'; done; done   # :prod digest = :X.Y.Z digest
```

The API and the gateway report the promoted staging SHA: deploy-prod retags
the staging images. The web reports the prod merge SHA. Both are correct.

Then check Better Stack for an API error, 5xx, or frontend-exception spike in
the minutes after the rollout.

`Deploy Prod` starts two mobile workflows on the deployed commit. `Mobile OTA`
publishes the JS bundle. `Mobile Store` builds and submits a new app version
when `apps/mobile/app.json` carries one: Android to the Play production track,
iOS to App Review with release after approval. Both must end green. A
`Mobile Store` warning asks for a version bump or a person in App Store
Connect (runbook: `apps/mobile/BUILD_GUIDE.md`). Both also run when
`Deploy Prod` failed only in its Kortix Capture or desktop installer builds
(`deploy-prod-gate.yml`); any other failed job stops them, and you then
dispatch them by hand once prod is live.

### Step 10 — self-host `:stable`

`:stable` moves **only** on the user's explicit, per-release consent — never
implied by "we released" or "prod is healthy." Run `promote-self-host-stable.yml`
by hand when that consent is given. It refuses a version with no published GitHub
Release `vX.Y.Z`: deploy-prod creates the Release only after prod served that
version, so `:stable` never names a version whose prod roll failed. `:latest`
and `:prod` move in deploy-prod's `promote-prod-channel` job, after
`verify-live-version`; `:X.Y.Z` exists from the retag on, because ECS rolls it.

### Step 11 — rollback

If a shipped version needs to come back: the **kortix-rollback** skill, not this
one. It is the inverse of Steps 7–9 (`rollback-prod.yml`, zero rebuild, the
frontend "clobber" trap, the DB-drift safety check).

## 3. Fix-forward traps

The failures that most often block Step 4 have known fixes. Read
[references/fix-forward-traps.md](references/fix-forward-traps.md) before
debugging one from scratch: out-of-order migration timestamps, stale
`mock.module` stubs after a refactor, source-anchor tests after a file move,
unintentional i18n catalog reordering, a stale `learnings/MEMORY.md`, and a
CodeQL alert in old code that a large diff surfaced for the first time — fix a
real finding on `dev`; dismiss a *proven* false positive on GitHub with a
written, evidence-backed justification, never silently.

## 4. Gotchas (hard-won)

- **deploy-prod concurrency = `cancel-in-progress: false`.** A slow desktop build or a
  zombie queued run blocks the next deploy — cancel it first. `rollback-prod.yml` uses
  the same group, so a rollback waits for a running deploy, and a waiting run of
  either one replaces the other's waiting run.
- **Any deploy-prod run undoes a rollback.** It re-rolls every ECS service to
  `prod:VERSION`. Do not dispatch it (for example with `rebuild_desktop`) while prod is
  rolled back, unless you mean to roll forward.
- **A release rebuilds the desktop app only when the desktop changed.** `desktop-plan`
  compares the desktop fingerprint with the latest release's `DESKTOP-FINGERPRINT`; when
  it is equal, `attach-desktop` copies that release's installers and `latest*.yml`, and
  installed apps get no update prompt. Force a build after rotating a signing certificate:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml --ref prod -f rebuild_desktop=true`
  (`apps/desktop-electron/README.md`, "A release ships a desktop update only when the
  desktop changed").
- **deploy-prod retags; it does not rebuild.** The staging build for the exact
  promoted commit must already be green:
  `gh run list --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --workflow build-staging.yml --branch staging --limit 3 --json status,conclusion,headSha`.
- **`/changelog` and `/changelog/releases` show every published `vX.Y.Z` release** and read
  GitHub Release bodies — so a thin/auto-generated body shows up as a thin entry. The weekly
  page reads only the bullets under `### New`, `### Improved` and `### Fixed`; a body without
  those headings shows as its title alone. Write real notes (Step 7).
- **VERSION is the source of truth**; the version field in `/v1/health` is stamped by
  deploy-prod's task-def, not baked into the image.
- **A promotion PR is not a normal PR.** Do not squash it, do not push new
  commits onto it to "fix" a failure — fix on `dev` and open a fresh promotion
  (Step 4). Squashing or force-pushing it breaks the SHA trail the migration
  cost pass and the release notes were verified against.
- **Private channels have their own rollout.** `KORTIX_PRIVATE_CHANNELS_ENABLED`
  stays unset until its checklist is done, and after it is on, no rollback goes
  below that release while a private channel exists. The checklist is
  [references/private-channels-rollout.md](references/private-channels-rollout.md).

## 5. Undo a bad / premature release

If a release was cut by mistake (and not yet truly published — i.e. no ECS roll / no
real Release), remove it cleanly. `dev` is protected from force-push, so revert there.
```bash
git push origin :refs/tags/vX.Y.Z                       # delete the tag
git push -f origin <prev-release-sha>:refs/heads/prod    # reset prod to the prior release
git revert --no-edit <version-bump-commit>               # put dev VERSION back; then push
gh release delete vX.Y.Z --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS           # only if a Release was actually cut
# cancel any deploy-prod the prod reset triggered
```
Verify: tag gone, `prod` VERSION = prior, `dev` VERSION = prior, api-prod unchanged,
no `vX.Y.Z` Release.

> Note: `prod` branch protection is `allow_force_pushes:false` + `enforce_admins:true`,
> so the `git push -f …:refs/heads/prod` above only works if protection is temporarily
> relaxed. For a release that's ALREADY LIVE, do NOT force-push — use the
> **kortix-rollback** skill instead.

## Checklist

1. Last nightly `Tests` run on `dev` checked; red lanes fixed on `dev` first.
   `bash scripts/pre-promote-tripwires.sh` green on the `dev` SHA you promote.
2. Every new migration in the diff costed read-only against prod before the dispatch.
3. `git log $PREV..origin/dev` read in full; title + notes written in
   kortix-voice, accurate to that log.
4. One `promote.yml` dispatch (`ref=dev`, title, notes); it merged into
   `staging`, staging served the SHA, and the release PR opened.
5. `full suite + quality gates` green on the release PR head (every check on
   that commit green); red fixed on `dev` and re-promoted with a new dispatch.
6. Release PR approved by a team member with write access (the releaser may approve), then
   merged into `prod` with `--merge` (`--admin` only with the
   owner's explicit OK).
7. `Deploy Prod` confirmed for the merge SHA; api/gateway/frontend `/health`,
   the three npm packages, the GitHub Release (24 assets), and Better Stack all
   verified on the new version; `Mobile OTA` and `Mobile Store` green.
8. `:stable` moved only if the user explicitly asked for it this release.
9. **One-time per env: the `/internal/*` edge key** (#9272, and the pentest
   2026-10-13 fix that made the API enforce it too). Done on dev; staging and
   prod are open until this runs. Two gates read the key: the api-router worker
   (`INTERNAL_EDGE_KEY`, 404s a public caller) and the API itself
   (`KORTIX_INTERNAL_EDGE_KEY`, 404s `/internal/gateway/*` without the header,
   which also covers the public backend origins such as
   `api-ecs-fargate.kortix.com` that skip the worker). The worker forwards the
   header. Do it after a release carrying the pentest fix is live in the env,
   in this order. A wrong order breaks LLM inference, because the gateway calls
   `/internal/gateway/*` through the public API host.
   1. Generate a random 32-byte key. Never print it.
   2. Add `KORTIX_INTERNAL_EDGE_KEY` to the env's Secrets Manager blob
      `kortix-<env>-env` in its `blob_region` region (the **dotenvx-secrets**
      skill, "Which region to edit"; needs an MFA session) and to
      `apps/api/.env.<env>` with `dotenvx set`.
   3. Redeploy the GATEWAY only (new ECS deployment). Confirm it sends the
      header: gateway `GET /v1/models` with a PAT still returns 200.
   4. Redeploy the API. It now enforces the key.
   5. `wrangler secret put INTERNAL_EDGE_KEY --env <env>` on the api-router
      worker, and redeploy the worker.
   6. Verify: `curl -X POST https://<api-host>/internal/gateway/authenticate`
      and the same on `/%69nternal/...` and on the backend origin host all
      return 404, and a gateway chat call gives the same answer as before.

# Kortix Release

How a clean, accurate production release happens. Three parts: **what version**
(the bump philosophy), **how a candidate gets tested** (one Promote dispatch takes
the `dev` HEAD through staging to a release PR; its one release suite is the
only gate), and **how prod gets it** (merge → deploy → verify). The release notes you write become the GitHub Release, which
the public **`/changelog/releases`** page (Release history) renders as written, and the
weekly **`/changelog`** page merges by section (New / Improved / Fixed) into the
week the release was published — so they must reflect what actually shipped,
nothing invented, nothing missed.

Pairs with **kortix-voice** (how the notes read) and **kortix-rollback** (the
reverse direction). The version source of truth is the root **`VERSION`** file;
`vX.Y.Z` tags are immutable and map 1:1 to a commit + image.

This file is the single source of truth for the promotion flow. `AGENTS.md`
(`CLAUDE.md`), `.agents/skills/contributing/SKILL.md`, and
`.agents/skills/testing/SKILL.md` state only their own slice — what CI runs on
a PR into `dev` versus the release PR — and point here for the rest.

## 0. Golden rule — one dispatch, one suite, one gate

**The only normal way to change prod is one Promote to Production dispatch.**
It takes the `dev` HEAD, merges it into `staging` itself (a PR that runs
nothing), waits until staging serves that SHA, and opens the release PR into
`prod`. That PR runs the **release suite** once: the contract lanes on the
release tree, the deployed smoke and the browser journeys against staging,
CI, CodeQL and the scanners. Its check `full suite + quality gates` requires
every one of them green, and it is the only check that blocks anything
(testing reset, 2026-10-16). Never `git push …:prod`, never open a manual PR
into `prod`, never cherry-pick onto `prod`.

Nothing else tests the release tree: no `Tests` run on a push to `dev`, no
check on the PR into `staging`. Staging is the deploy target the suite runs
against, not a test stage. The nightly `Tests` run on `dev` (contract lanes,
no browser) warns early: check it before you promote, and fix `dev` forward
when it is red, because the release suite fails on the same lanes.

`dev` is the dev trunk. It can move fast and can temporarily be broken.
Production promotion always reads from `staging`.

## 1. Versioning philosophy — what bump?

Semver `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. **Default to patch.** When unsure, patch.

- **Patch** (`1.0.0 → 1.0.1`) — the everyday release. Bug fixes, small features,
  copy, docs, infra, polish. **This is most releases.** Ship often; keep them small.
- **Minor** (`1.0.x → 1.1.0`) — a milestone worth signposting: a meaningful batch of
  new user-facing capability. Use sparingly, when a release is genuinely "a thing."
- **Major** (`1.x → 2.0.0`) — a breaking change or an architecture shift (the kind of
  jump v0.x → 1.0 was). Rare.

If the change set is "fixes + a couple small features" → **patch**. Don't inflate.

## 2. The flow (do this every time)

### Step 1 — `dev` takes verified merges; the nightly run warns

`dev` takes PRs with no required CI: the developer verifies the change by
using it (the **testing** skill). A push to `dev` runs no `Tests` lane. The
nightly run on `dev` (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`, 05:41 UTC) comments a red
result on the commit. Fix it forward on `dev`, or revert the culprit after 1 hour.

### Step 2 — check the nightly run and cost migrations

```bash
gh run list --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --workflow tests.yml --branch dev --event schedule \
  --limit 1 --json conclusion,headSha --jq '.[0]'
```

A red night means fix `dev` first. Then cost every new migration (Step 5)
before you dispatch: Promote applies it to the staging database within minutes.

Then run the release suite's fast tripwires on the `dev` SHA you promote:

```bash
git fetch origin dev && git switch --detach origin/dev   # in your own worktree
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && bash scripts/pre-promote-tripwires.sh
```

It takes about 2.5 min. It names each red check, and you fix each one on
`dev` before the dispatch. v0.15.11 needed 3 release-suite runs (about 1 h
each) for failures this script finds in minutes (the learnings ledger,
2026-11-14).

The script runs no DB suite and only a few package tests. When the last
nightly is red, or `dev` moved since it ran, also run the contract lanes on
the `dev` SHA you promote (about 15 min) and fix every red lane first:

```bash
gh workflow run tests.yml --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --ref dev
```

v0.16.5 found 6 reds this way that the script missed (the learnings ledger,
2026-11-24).

### Step 3 — one dispatch: Promote to Production

Write the title and notes (Step 7 shows how), then:

```bash
gh workflow run promote.yml --repo kortix-ai/CompanyOS --ref dev \
  -f ref=dev -f title="<title>" -f notes="$(cat <<'EOF'
<markdown notes>
EOF
)" -f bump=patch
```

Promote then:

1. Resolves `ref` (default `dev`) to a SHA and pushes it to
   `promote/dev-<sha10>`. On a conflict with `staging` it builds the branch as
   a merge whose tree equals the dev SHA's tree (`git read-tree --reset -u`).
2. Opens the PR into `staging` and merges it as a merge commit (never squash).
   That PR runs no check.
3. Dispatches `build-staging.yml` for the merge SHA (a merge made with the
   workflow token starts no push workflow), waits for Build and Deploy
   Staging, then needs 8 consecutive `/health` reads where API, gateway and web
   all serve the merge SHA.
4. Creates or updates `release/vX.Y.Z`, opens the PR into `prod`, and approves
   the held runs on it, so the release suite starts.

`-f dry_run=true` prints every decision (SHA, conflict, PR, version) and
changes nothing. `-f ref=staging` skips the dev leg: the hotfix path for a
commit already on `staging`.

**A failed promote resumes.** When the run fails after the staging merge
(build, deploy or the `/health` proof), fix the cause and re-run the run (or
dispatch again with the same `ref`). The plan step finds the merged
`promote/dev-<sha10>` PR; while its merge is still the staging tip it skips the
merge, skips the build when the three staging manifests already passed, and
always repeats the 8-read `/health` proof. When staging moved on after that
merge, use `-f ref=staging`. A re-promote cancels the gate run of the release
PR's older head itself.

Merge only when `full suite + quality gates` is green on the release PR's head
SHA. Never fix on the release or promotion branch, and never weaken a check
(the fix-forward traps are in
[references/fix-forward-traps.md](references/fix-forward-traps.md)).

**The candidate is frozen on `staging`.** A red suite is fixed on the tree
that was promoted, not on a newer `dev`: every re-promote from `dev` pulls in
new merges, and on 2026-10-28 five cycles in a row each failed on new `dev`
drift (Marko: "pin it to whatever got promoted to staging & fix it on staging
until it's green"). Per fix:

1. Merge the fix into `dev` through a PR, as usual, so `dev` keeps it.
2. Cherry-pick that commit onto `staging` through a PR:
   `git switch -c stage-fix/<slug> origin/staging && git cherry-pick <dev sha>`.
   Then regenerate the generated files on that branch and commit any change:
   `bash .agents/skills/learnings/scripts/index.sh` and
   `node packages/ui/scripts/gen-i18n-catalog.mjs`. `dev`'s copy can list an
   entry or a key from a commit that `staging` lacks (the learnings ledger,
   2026-11-02). Push, `gh pr create --base staging`, `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   The push to `staging` starts Build Staging and Deploy Staging.
3. When `/health` on the three staging surfaces serves the new staging SHA,
   dispatch `promote.yml -f ref=staging` (no `dev` leg). It updates the
   release branch, and the suite runs once on the new tree.

The next normal Promote from `dev` merges cleanly: `dev` already holds every
fix that `staging` got.

### Step 5 — cost every new migration against prod, before merging

For every migration file new in the diff versus what's already applied to prod
(`select name from kortix_migrations.pgmigrations order by id desc limit 5;` on
the real prod database), run it read-only against prod first:

```bash
PGOPTIONS='-c default_transaction_read_only=on -c statement_timeout=15000' \
  psql "$PROD_DATABASE_URL" -c "explain (analyze, buffers) <the migration's statement, read-only form>"
```

judging a migration safe. Pre-build any large `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` out of
band on prod, with the migration's **exact** statement, so the real deploy step
is a no-op (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` on an index that already
exists does nothing). If the deploy step still hits `55P03` (lock timeout),
**retry by rerunning the migration job** — never by raising `lock_timeout` in a
plain migration (the **learnings** ledger, "Retry a hot-table ADD COLUMN that
hit its 2 s lock_timeout; never raise the timeout", 2026-09-25). Full costing
method: §4 "Gotchas" below and `packages/db/MIGRATIONS.md`.

### Step 6 — staging deploy

Promote dispatches `Build Staging Artifacts`, which starts `Deploy Staging`:
it applies pending migrations to the staging database and rolls staging.
Promote waits for the proof itself; to check by hand:

```bash
curl -fsS https://staging-api.kortix.com/v1/health | jq '{environment,version,commit}'
curl -fsS https://gateway-staging.kortix.com/health/live | jq '{version,commit}'
```

The gateway's `/health` answers only `{status}` to an anonymous caller
(`apps/llm-gateway/src/health.test.ts`); `/health/live` carries the version.
The staging web sits behind Vercel Authentication: an anonymous read of
`staging.kortix.com/api/health` gets `302`. Promote reads it with the Vercel

points at `dev.kortix.com` / `dev-api.kortix.com` is a broken staging setup, not
a passing gate.

not from memory:

```bash
git fetch origin --tags --quiet
PREV="$(git tag -l 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1)"
git log "$PREV..origin/dev" --no-merges --pretty='- %s (%h)'

- **notes** — markdown bullets grouped loosely (new / improved / fixed),

  Follow **kortix-voice**: plain language, no hype, "open source" never a
  license name. Every notable commit in the log maps to a line in the notes;
  nothing invented, nothing dropped — the notes are the public `/changelog`.

Then run:

iOS to App Review with release after approval. Both must end green. A
`Mobile Store` warning asks for a version bump or a person in App Store
Connect (runbook: `apps/mobile/BUILD_GUIDE.md`). Both also run when
`Deploy Prod` failed only in its Kortix Capture or desktop installer builds
(`deploy-prod-gate.yml`); any other failed job stops them, and you then
dispatch them by hand once prod is live.
